about_lede: MicroMatch is a free, non-commercial student project. It launches first at Wesleyan.
about_meta_description: MicroMatch is a free, non-commercial student project that turns small nonprofit jobs into 5 to 30 minute tasks, launching first at Wesleyan.
about_person_body: Directories hand you an email address and disappear. Here the work happens on the site: you claim a task, send your work, and someone at the nonprofit reads it. That review is what makes a patch mean something.
about_person_title: Why a person checks every one
about_quilt_body: A quilt is many small pieces, cut by different hands, that only become warm once someone sews them together. Each approved task is one piece. The quilt on this site is built from those approvals and nothing else.
about_runs_code: The code is open under the MIT license on <github>GitHub</github>. See <privacy>the privacy policy</privacy> for what each service handles.
about_runs_hosting: Hosting on Vercel. Accounts, data and files in Appwrite.
about_runs_propublica: Nonprofit checks against the ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer for US organizations.
about_runs_safety: Azure AI Content Safety on task text and claim notes.
about_runs_translate: A self-hosted LibreTranslate server for task text in other languages.
about_why_body: Most volunteering asks for a Saturday morning or a semester. Plenty of people have fifteen minutes instead, and plenty of nonprofits have jobs that size waiting: a flyer to translate, alt text to check, photos to tag. MicroMatch puts the two together.

docs_badges_1: Each nonprofit designs its badges: a name, a color and an icon. A badge has one of two rules: it is awarded for any completed task you posted, or for one task you choose. When you approve a claim, every badge whose rule matches is awarded, and a volunteer never gets the same badge twice.
docs_badges_2: The patch sewn into the quilt for an approved claim wears that badge's color and icon: the badge for that exact task first, otherwise your any-task badge. With no badge designed, the patch is plain, undyed cloth.

docs_ngo_post_body: Give each task one clear outcome: what to make, what done looks like, and anything the volunteer needs. Estimate honestly between 5 and 30 minutes. Add tags, and a deadline or volunteer cap if you need them.
docs_ngo_review_body: Claims on your tasks wait in your reviews with the volunteer's link and note. Approve to award your badges, or reject if the work is not what you needed.

docs_ngo_verify_4: You get an email with the decision. Once approved, your tasks appear in the feed with the verified mark.

help_a_rejected: You get an email with the reviewer's reason. Update your details or upload another document from your account and send it again. The decision is saved even if the email does not arrive.
help_a_review: A person at the nonprofit reviews each claim, so it depends on them. Your claim stays pinned to your block until they approve or reject it.
help_a_switch: Yes, from your profile. Switching from nonprofit to volunteer withdraws any verification application and removes the verified mark from tasks you posted.

home_meta_description_q: Nonprofits post tasks that take 5 to 30 minutes. Volunteers do one, a person approves it, and it becomes a patch in a shared community quilt.
home_meta_title_q: MicroMatch: small volunteer tasks, sewn into one quilt
how_lede: Every patch on the quilt went through the same four steps, and a person checked it at the last one.
how_meta_description: Four steps from a posted task to a patch sewn into the quilt: a nonprofit posts it, you pick it up, you pin your proof, and a person approves it.
how_meta_title: How a patch is made | MicroMatch
how_step_1_body: A verified nonprofit posts a task: a title, a short summary, the full brief and an honest estimate between 5 and 30 minutes. It can add tags, a deadline and a cap on how many volunteers it needs. Task text goes through Azure AI Content Safety before it is saved.
how_step_1_note: Only tasks from verified nonprofits appear in the feed.
how_step_2_body: Browse the <feed>task feed</feed> without an account. Search it, filter it to 15, 20 or 30 minutes, or narrow it by tag. When one fits the time you have, open it and claim it. Claiming needs an account.
how_step_3_body: Do the task, then send your proof: a link to what you made (a document, a shared folder, a pull request) and a note about how you did it. Your claim is pinned, not sewn: it waits for a person at the nonprofit.
how_step_3_title: You pin your work to it
how_step_4_body: Someone at the nonprofit reads your proof and approves the claim, or rejects it if it is not what they needed. Approval awards the badges that nonprofit designed, for any task it posted or for that one task, and your patch is sewn into the community block in their colors.
how_step_4_note: No points, levels or streaks. A patch means one finished task, checked by a person.

nonprofits_design_title: Design the patch your volunteers earn
nonprofits_free: MicroMatch is free and non-commercial. There is nothing to pay.
nonprofits_lede: Post the small jobs that sit at the bottom of your list. A volunteer does one in 5 to 30 minutes, and someone on your team checks it.
nonprofits_meta_description: Post the small jobs on your list as 5 to 30 minute tasks. A person on your team approves each one, and volunteers earn the patch you design.
nonprofits_post_body: A title, a one-line summary, the full brief and an honest estimate from 5 to 30 minutes. Add tags so people can find it, and a deadline or a cap on how many volunteers you need if that matters. Task text goes through Azure AI Content Safety before it is saved.
nonprofits_review_body: Each claim arrives with a link to the work and the volunteer's note. Approve it and your patch is awarded and sewn into the quilt; reject it if it is not what you needed. Nothing is approved automatically.
nonprofits_verify_1: Send your organization's name, country and tax or charity registration number.
nonprofits_verify_2: For a US EIN, an admin checks it against the ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer. Outside the US, upload a registration document (PDF, PNG or JPEG) for an admin to review.
nonprofits_verify_3: You get an email when an admin approves or rejects your application, with the reason if it was rejected.
nonprofits_verify_4: Until you are verified, your tasks stay out of the public feed. Once you are, every task you have posted shows the verified mark.
